steps: A real static Scene2D build plan reports the actor speed diagnostic with exact provenance. Its source action opens the BOM/CRLF document, retains diagnostic code/message/path beside the editor, and selects the exact JSON string. Independent full-text DOM Range measurement confirms visibility after a long CJK/emoji soft-wrapped title. No engine is executed.

The diagnostic panel and collapsible details only display information: no input event, dirty state, document save, or author file write. The oversized title is a separate intentional fixture diagnostic; the selected target is /actors/0/speed.
Typing a numeric speed marks the displayed diagnosis as needing a new check. Native Undo restores every source character but conservatively leaves the old diagnosis marked changed.

Chinese, English and Japanese diagnostic panels fit 390px with a scrollable source pane and a usable editor. Scrolling the panel into view exposes the entire dismiss control. Language changes preserve selection/content, and the original edit still redoes and undoes natively.

Switching to another document clears the displayed diagnostic. Reopening the current plan restores an exact current-source diagnosis. Dismiss changes only the panel, preserving source, selection, dirty state, requests and author files.

Only ordinary Save persists the numeric speed edit: exactly one source save, only the target scene changed, BOM and CRLF retained, and the editor returns clean. Registry/templates/assets remain identical. The build service still holds only its original static plan, with no generated or executed engine project.
